concepts.title: Equally likely outcomes
concepts.explanation: When all elementary outcomes are equally likely, P(E) = favourable outcomes / total outcomes. List outcomes before counting.

example.problem: Choose uniformly an integer from 1 to 12, inclusive. Find P(a multiple of 3).
steps: There are 4 multiples of 3 among 12 integers.

concepts.commonMistake: The counting formula needs equally likely outcomes; not all verbal categories are equally likely.

concepts.title: Complementary events
concepts.explanation: An event and its complement cover every outcome without overlap, so P(not E) = 1 − P(E). Probabilities lie between 0 and 1.

example.problem: A bag has 2 red and 5 blue balls, all equally likely to be drawn. Find P(not red).

concepts.commonMistake: The complement of at least one is none, not exactly one.

concepts.title: Random draws
concepts.explanation: For a uniformly chosen ball or numbered card, count the objects that satisfy the condition and divide by the total number of objects.

example.problem: Cards numbered 1 to 10 are equally likely to be drawn. Find P(a number greater than 6).
steps: There are 4 qualifying cards out of 10.

concepts.commonMistake: Objects are counted, not just the number of colour categories.

concepts.title: Coin sample spaces
concepts.explanation: Independent fair coin tosses have equally likely ordered H/T sequences. Enumerate them or count positions when calculating an event.

example.problem: Toss 2 independent fair coins. Find P(exactly one head).
steps: The head can occupy 2 positions among 4 sequences.

concepts.commonMistake: HH, HT, TH and TT are four outcomes; one-head is not a single elementary outcome.
checklist: Apply exactly, at least, or at most carefully.

concepts.title: Two-dice sample spaces
concepts.explanation: Two independent fair six-sided dice have 36 equally likely ordered outcomes. Sums are not equally likely; count the ordered pairs that produce the event.

example.problem: Two independent fair dice are rolled. Find P(both scores ≤ 2).
steps: Each die has 2 qualifying scores, giving 4 ordered pairs.

questions.prompt: A fair six-sided die is rolled. Find P(score ≤ 2).
questions.explanation: Favourable scores are 1 through 2: 2 out of 6. Probability = 1/3.

questions.prompt: A fair six-sided die is rolled. Find P(score ≤ 3).
questions.explanation: Favourable scores are 1 through 3: 3 out of 6. Probability = 1/2.

questions.prompt: A fair six-sided die is rolled. Find P(score ≤ 4).
questions.explanation: Favourable scores are 1 through 4: 4 out of 6. Probability = 2/3.

questions.prompt: Choose uniformly an integer from 1 to 12, inclusive. Find P(a multiple of 3).
questions.explanation: There are 4 multiples of 3 among 12 integers. Probability = 1/3.

questions.prompt: Choose uniformly an integer from 1 to 18, inclusive. Find P(a multiple of 3).
questions.explanation: There are 6 multiples of 3 among 18 integers. Probability = 1/3.

questions.prompt: Choose uniformly an integer from 1 to 24, inclusive. Find P(a multiple of 3).
questions.explanation: There are 8 multiples of 3 among 24 integers. Probability = 1/3.

questions.prompt: Choose uniformly an integer from 1 to 12, inclusive. Find P(divisible by 2 or 3).
questions.explanation: Count multiples: 6 of 2, 4 of 3; subtract 2 multiples of 6 counted twice. Probability = 8/12 = 2/3.

questions.prompt: Choose uniformly an integer from 1 to 18, inclusive. Find P(divisible by 2 or 3).
questions.explanation: Count multiples: 9 of 2, 6 of 3; subtract 3 multiples of 6 counted twice. Probability = 12/18 = 2/3.

questions.prompt: Choose uniformly an integer from 1 to 24, inclusive. Find P(divisible by 2 or 3).
questions.explanation: Count multiples: 12 of 2, 8 of 3; subtract 4 multiples of 6 counted twice. Probability = 16/24 = 2/3.

A bag has 2 red and 5 blue balls, all equally likely to be drawn. Find P(not red).
questions.explanation: There are 7 balls. P(not red) = 1 − 2/7 = 5/7.

questions.prompt: A bag has 3 red and 7 blue balls, all equally likely to be drawn. Find P(not red).
questions.explanation: There are 10 balls. P(not red) = 1 − 3/10 = 7/10.

questions.prompt: A bag has 4 red and 9 blue balls, all equally likely to be drawn. Find P(not red).
questions.explanation: There are 13 balls. P(not red) = 1 − 4/13 = 9/13.

questions.prompt: Toss 2 independent fair coins. Find P(at least one head).
questions.explanation: The complement is all tails: one sequence out of 4. Probability = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.prompt: Toss 3 independent fair coins. Find P(at least one head).
questions.explanation: The complement is all tails: one sequence out of 8. Probability = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8.

questions.prompt: Toss 4 independent fair coins. Find P(at least one head).
questions.explanation: The complement is all tails: one sequence out of 16. Probability = 1 − 1/16 = 15/16.

questions.prompt: A bag has 2 white and 5 black balls. Draw one uniformly. Find P(black).
questions.explanation: Total = 7; black = 5. P = 5/7.

questions.prompt: A bag has 3 white and 6 black balls. Draw one uniformly. Find P(black).
questions.explanation: Total = 9; black = 6. P = 2/3.

questions.prompt: A bag has 4 white and 7 black balls. Draw one uniformly. Find P(black).
questions.explanation: Total = 11; black = 7. P = 7/11.

questions.prompt: Cards numbered 1 to 10 are equally likely to be drawn. Find P(a number greater than 6).
questions.explanation: There are 4 qualifying cards out of 10. Probability = 2/5.

questions.prompt: Cards numbered 1 to 15 are equally likely to be drawn. Find P(a number greater than 9).
questions.explanation: There are 6 qualifying cards out of 15. Probability = 2/5.

questions.prompt: Cards numbered 1 to 20 are equally likely to be drawn. Find P(a number greater than 12).
questions.explanation: There are 8 qualifying cards out of 20. Probability = 2/5.

questions.prompt: A bag starts with 2 red and 4 blue balls. How many red balls must be added to make P(red) = 1/2 on a uniform draw?
questions.explanation: Red and blue counts must become equal. Add 4 − 2 = 2 red balls.

questions.prompt: A bag starts with 3 red and 6 blue balls. How many red balls must be added to make P(red) = 1/2 on a uniform draw?
questions.explanation: Red and blue counts must become equal. Add 6 − 3 = 3 red balls.

questions.prompt: A bag starts with 4 red and 8 blue balls. How many red balls must be added to make P(red) = 1/2 on a uniform draw?
questions.explanation: Red and blue counts must become equal. Add 8 − 4 = 4 red balls.

questions.prompt: Toss 2 independent fair coins. How many equally likely ordered sequences are possible?
questions.explanation: Two choices for each coin gives 2^2 = 4.

questions.prompt: Toss 3 independent fair coins. How many equally likely ordered sequences are possible?
questions.explanation: Two choices for each coin gives 2^3 = 8.

questions.prompt: Toss 4 independent fair coins. How many equally likely ordered sequences are possible?
questions.explanation: Two choices for each coin gives 2^4 = 16.

questions.prompt: Toss 2 independent fair coins. Find P(exactly one head).

questions.prompt: Toss 4 independent fair coins. Find P(exactly one head).
questions.explanation: The head can occupy 4 positions among 16 sequences. Probability = 1/4.

questions.prompt: Toss 2 independent fair coins. Find P(at most one head).
questions.explanation: One all-tail sequence plus 2 one-head sequences gives 3 favourable outcomes. Probability = 3/4.

questions.prompt: Toss 3 independent fair coins. Find P(at most one head).
questions.explanation: One all-tail sequence plus 3 one-head sequences gives 4 favourable outcomes. Probability = 1/2.

questions.prompt: Toss 4 independent fair coins. Find P(at most one head).
questions.explanation: One all-tail sequence plus 4 one-head sequences gives 5 favourable outcomes. Probability = 5/16.
